title: Pack a grocery tote with the eggs on top of the cans
instruction: Pack the two cans and the egg carton into the tote, with the eggs on top of the cans.
context: Grocery packers and online-order pickers load heavy items first and fragile ones last, on top; picking up whatever is nearest first puts cans on the eggs. Done by: hand packers and packagers, online grocery order pickers.
setup: An open dark grey polypropylene tote is fixed to the table between the arms, its centre 24 cm in front of the arm bases: inside 16 cm front to back, 10 cm side to side, walls 6 cm tall and 5 mm thick, a 4 mm floor. Two red steel food cans (7 cm diameter, 8 cm tall, 400 g each) stand upright in front of the left arm, 30 cm left of centre, their centres 20 and 32 cm in front of the arm bases. A blue plastic carton of six eggs (14 cm long, 8 cm wide, 6 cm tall, 400 g) lies flat in front of the right arm, 30 cm right of centre, its centre 25 cm in front of the arm bases, its long side pointing away from the arms. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A can counts as in the tote when its centre is inside the tote's inner outline (or within 5 mm past it, leaning on a wall) and its bottom is no lower than the tote's floor: 0.2 each. The carton is on top when it is in the tote the same way, tilted at most 10 degrees, its bottom no more than 1 cm below the higher can's top, with both cans in the tote and the carton still: 0.6. If the carton is in the tote and tilted at most 30 degrees but not on top: 0.1 instead. All of it, both cans in and the carton on top: 1.0. If a can ends up resting on the carton (its bottom within 1 cm of the carton's top or above it, over the carton), the score is 0.
reset_notes: Stand the cans back at their marks in front of the left arm and lay the carton flat at its mark in front of the right arm, long side pointing away from the arms; tape outlines on the table make this quick.
fidelity: Approximate: the carton is one rigid box, so the eggs inside aren't modelled and nothing breaks; a can resting on the carton stands in for crushed eggs. The cans are solid cylinders. The tote is fixed in place (clamp or tape it down for real trials). Every object, the tote included, has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than steel or plastic.
